neighbours.label: the name of a classical or medieval geographer or historian cited as the source for a place ('according to Herodotus', 'Strabo describes', 'the medieval geographers'), against modern sources in the same citation frame
fire: The harbor, as Herodotus tells us, was guarded by a great bronze chain.
The tribes beyond the river, Strabo writes, lived in wagons and tents.
Arab geographers of the tenth century placed the market near the delta.
The town is described by Diodorus as rich in olives and horses.
Some classical geographers believed the river flowed out of a lake.
In Herodotus the island is called by a different and older name.
The pass, according to Strabo, was only wide enough for one wagon.
Medieval geographers reported that the fortress had seven iron gates.
quiet: The harbor, as the guidebook tells us, was dredged in the last century.
The tribes beyond the river, the reporter writes, now farm cotton.
Local surveyors of the last century placed the market near the delta.
The town is described by the tourist board as rich in olives and horses.
Some modern engineers believed the river could be dammed upstream.
In the new brochure the island is called by a shorter name.
The pass, according to the park rangers, closes every November.
City officials reported that the stadium had seven new gates.
